_README: R-8 §13. The human half of scripts/preflight.mjs.
Each key below is something no program can establish from inside a
process: a DNS record resolving, a certificate terminating, a restore
actually performed, an SMS reaching a handset, a push landing on a phone,
an alert waking a person, a school completing an onboarding. The preflight
checks whether the CONFIGURATION for each exists; this file records
whether the THING actually happened, and WHERE.
Shape, per R-8 §13:
status       null | "rehearsed" | "verified"
date         ISO date the observation was made
environment  the deployment it was observed on, verbatim
evidence     what was actually seen — numbers, not adjectives
result       "pass" | "fail"
THE ENVIRONMENT FIELD IS LOAD-BEARING. The preflight compares it against
the deployment being checked and treats a mismatch as UNVERIFIED. That is
deliberate: a restore rehearsed on a laptop is real work and worth
recording, and it is NOT a production restore. An evidence file that could
not tell those apart would let a rehearsal close a production gate, which
is the exact failure this mechanism exists to prevent.
Rules:
- null means never tested. Keep it null. A null is worth more than a
confident guess, and every one of these was null before it was earned.
- Never fill an entry from configuration intent. "The provider is
configured" is not "a message arrived".
- Attestations lapse after 180 days: "we restored a backup successfully"
stops being a fact about the current system fairly quickly.
- status "rehearsed" means the procedure was executed somewhere that is
not the target environment. It closes no production gate. It exists so
the production run is a repeat of a rehearsed thing rather than a first
attempt during an incident.
- status "blocked" means it was ATTEMPTED and could not be completed,
with the obstacle recorded. result stays null, so it closes nothing —
but "we tried on this date and here is exactly what stopped us" is
worth more to the next person than a bare null, and it stops the same
dead end being walked into twice.

real_push_delivery.evidence: Production now has a real HTTPS origin (https://sikhon.systems, valid Let's Encrypt cert) with real VAPID keys configured, so the earlier blocker (no secure real-device target) is removed. Remaining: the full subscribe -> publish -> deliver -> click -> branding -> unsubscribe flow needs (a) a notifications-granted real browser and (b) an onboarded tenant with a notice to publish. It is now a ~10-minute manual test from any ordinary Chrome/Edge/Firefox once a pilot school exists. Do not mark pass until a real push is observed on a device.

backup_configured.evidence: Daily pg_dump -Fc of shikhon_lms via /usr/local/bin/shikhon-backup.sh (cron 02:30), 14-day retention in /var/backups/shikhon. First backup taken and confirmed (913K). RPO is bounded by the daily schedule; tighten to hourly before real student data lands.

restore_drill.evidence: scripts/restore-drill.mjs against the PRODUCTION shikhon-postgres container: pg_dump -Fc (0.8 MB) -> restore into an isolated database -> 7 schema counts (121 tables, 227 RLS policies, functions, triggers, partitions) and 27 table counts identical to source. RTO 1.5s (on a near-empty pre-pilot DB; re-measure at pilot size). Supersedes the 2026-08-30 local-docker rehearsal.

prod_cross_tenant.evidence: scripts/security-probe.mjs — 29 of 29 checks across 12 areas against a running deployment, positive and negative cases, none failing, none skipped. Covers: positive control (roster, sync/pull, dashboard all serve the right school); forged X-Tenant-ID/X-User-ID/X-Role ignored in favour of signed claims; headers-without-token and garbage-bearer both 401; cross-tenant reads of section, student and attendance by id refused; a cross-tenant WRITE through a payload tenantId not applied; no runtime role holds SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS; tenant A's DB context cannot see tenant B's rows by primary key while still seeing its own; no tenant context set means nothing visible; every table carrying tenant_id has RLS enabled; a service credential from a browser refused; a user token is not a service credential and cannot run maintenance; 7 hostile push endpoints (http, loopback, 169.254.169.254, private range, userinfo, .internal, .local) all refused; cross-tenant notice and document access refused; the platform health endpoint unreachable with a tenant token; the console refuses both a tenant user and an anonymous caller; no live secret value or connection string in app.js/platform.js/sw.js; error bodies carry no credential; an unlisted CORS origin is not echoed and credentials are never allowed; per-phone OTP requests are rate-limited. A production deployment now exists (https://sikhon.systems), but its database has 0 tenants, so this two-tenant probe cannot run there yet; re-run against production once the first pilot schools are onboarded. The DB-level RLS posture WAS verified on production directly: shikhon_app/platform are non-superuser non-bypassrls, and shikhon_app sees 0 tenants with no context set.

production_deployment.evidence: Live at https://sikhon.systems on a Hostinger KVM2 VPS (Ubuntu 24.04, 200.234.43.179), deployed commit 52d1609 via git archive (the verified local tree, NOT the stale GitHub snapshots). Node 22.23 systemd service (unprivileged user) on 172.16.1.1:4100; isolated pgvector 0.8.6 container (shikhon_lms, 48 migrations, 227 RLS policies, shikhon_app/platform non-superuser non-bypassrls, 0 tenants visible with no context); Caddy reverse-proxy with a valid Let's Encrypt cert (CN=sikhon.systems, through 2026-11-29). Browser-verified: /, /app, /platform all 200 with zero console errors; API auth 401 unauth / 200 public; sibling apps on the shared box unaffected. NOT a full pilot readiness — see the null items below.
